title: Your first verses: Bismillah and al-Hamdu lillah
hook: Read the first two verses of al-Fatiha, word by word.

screens.text: **You can read this now.** Almost every letter and mark in the first two verses of al-Fatiha is one you know, plus three small new ones today. Then you read them, one word at a time.
**Allah: الله.** Alif, laam, laam, haa. The two laams merge into one held sound: al-laah. You have said this word in every prayer. Now you can read it.

cards.back: bismi-llaahi: the alif with a small sign on top (ٱ, alif wasla) is silent when it joins the word before
ar-raḥmaan: the small upright alif above the m is a long aa, just like ا
al-ʿaalamiin: the flat line after ع only stretches the join and has no sound. The small alif on it is a long aa

screens.text: **Bismillah, word by word.** The first verse of al-Fatiha has four words [Q 1:1]. Tap each card to see how it sounds.

screens.prompt: Which word is ar-raḥiim (the Especially Merciful)?

options.feedback: Yes. Spot the long ee (kasra + yaa) before the final m.
That's ar-raḥmaan: look for the small upright alif (long aa) above the m.
That's bismi: in the name of.

screens.text: **Verse two [Q 1:2]:** al-ḥamdu lillaahi rabbi l-ʿaalamiin. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. Spot the shadda in rabbi from lesson 10.

options.feedback: Yes: rabbi l-ʿaalamiin, Lord of the worlds.
That word ends verse one. Verse two ends with the worlds.
Bismi starts verse one. Verse two ends with the worlds.

chips: How do I keep learning to read the Quran?
What's tajweed, and do I need it?
Is it okay to read slowly for now?

screens.text: Open the Quran to al-Fatiha and read the first two verses slowly, word by word.
You read Allah, Bismillah and al-Hamdu lillah from the Arabic. Slow is fine. Every reader started here.
From not knowing a letter to reading al-Fatiha's first verses. Keep going, a few minutes at a time.

options.feedback: That's not it. Look for two laams and a haa.

check.prompt: How should you read when you're starting out?

options.feedback: No need. Slow and careful is how everyone starts.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Allah (الله): alif, laam, laam, haa; the laam is doubled and read full.
- Q 1:1 (Bismillah) and Q 1:2 (al-Hamdu lillah), word by word, from the Citation Bank text.
- Meanings follow Saheeh International: "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful"; "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds".
- No audio for the verses in this lesson. For recitation, point to quran.com audio and a teacher at the masjid.

**Likely questions**
- *"Do I need to read Arabic to pray?"* No. The main path teaches the prayer's phrases by heart, with transliteration. Reading helps over time.
- *"Can I learn from transliteration for now?"* Yes, as a bridge. Encourage moving to the Arabic script bit by bit, and learning with a teacher at the masjid.
- *"Does a pronunciation mistake ruin my prayer?"* A question for the imam: offer "Ask my imam". Learners are expected to be learning.

**Escalate:** tajweed rules beyond this lesson; whether specific recitation mistakes affect the prayer.

**Don't**
- Don't add rules this lesson hasn't taught.
- Don't make the convert feel behind. This track is optional.

- Qur'an [1:1](https://quran.com/1/1), [1:2](https://quran.com/1/2), Saheeh International translation.
